notes: Each eval gives the agent a prompt and a fixture folder. Grade the answer against must / must_not. An eval passes when every 'must' item is met and no 'must_not' item happens.

evals.prompt: A user picked two favourite venues and Concerts, but the list shows concerts at other venues. Only Concerts works. We fixed this area yesterday. Verify the bug and propose a fix.
must: Says the request can end with an empty venue_ids list and that the API reads empty as 'any venue'
Names the previous fix (dropping id 0) as the cause or first suspect
Flags id 0 as a sentinel colliding with real venues
Proposes a fix that keeps the user's selection and shows an honest empty state instead of calling the API without the filter
Names a backend/CMS finding with an owner (venues with id 0 / no linked events)
Builds an impact map with at least: linked venues only, unlinked only, mixed, no favourite venue
must_not: Proposes sending id 0 again as the whole fix
Marks the bug Verified without a reproduction, oracle request or concrete code trigger

must: Flags that refresh() uses PUT with no body to read the account
Explains at least one consequence: needs update permission, touches the last-updated timestamp, or risk of overwriting data
Proposes a read endpoint (GET) and says to confirm it returns the same fields
must_not: Reports the PUT in save() as a bug

evals.prompt: Some users always see 'Something went wrong' on every Home list. Others never do. Find out why.
must: Says an empty result is shown as an error
Uses combinations.csv (or proposes a combination sweep) to show that some venue x category pairs have no events
Proposes a Home fallback (widen the query step by step) or an honest empty state, and explains why Home may widen while an explicit filter must not
must_not: Blames the network or the server being down without evidence

evals.prompt: App Review rejected our build: the app does not open. It works on my phone with the build from last month. Get it ready for resubmission.
must: Identifies the missing UIScene life cycle (no UIApplicationSceneManifest / SceneDelegate) as a launch blocker for the new SDK
Says to build and launch with the same Xcode/SDK used for submission on the newest OS before resubmitting
Notes that the social login URL handling must move to the scene delegate and be retested
must_not: Concludes the reviewer's device was at fault without checking the toolchain

evals.prompt: Audit privacy in the account screen and analytics before release.
must: Flags that the tracking switch never opts the analytics SDK out
Flags that logout does not reset the analytics identity (identified by email)
Flags the response store in Documents (backed up) that stores every response, including writes, and survives logout
Flags that the switch state and event are not reverted / logged only on a successful save
must_not: Prints or invents real tokens or emails

evals.prompt: app-a crashes in KeyboardAvoiding.keyboardWillHide in production. Fix it. app-b is a sibling app from the same codebase.
must: Explains that willHide can arrive without willShow, so the force unwrap crashes
Fix restores the size only if one was saved, with no visual change
Checks app-b and reports the same bug there
must_not: Fixes only app-a without mentioning app-b

evals.prompt: Users say lists sometimes load forever and sometimes show the wrong picture. Audit the networking and image code.
must: Flags that failures only print and never call completion (endless spinner)
Flags that the HTTP status is never checked, so a decodable error body is treated as success
Flags that a late image can be applied to a reused cell
Mentions the blocking Data(contentsOf:) download and memory-only/no caching
must_not: Marks these as Verified on device without having run a device

evals.prompt: A user says saving the profile does not work. Verify it.
must: Concludes the bug is not reproduced and keeps it Suspected (not Verified, not 'not a bug')
Asks only for what is missing: app version and build, device/OS, exact field edited, the error shown, time of the attempt
Lists the checks already done (code path, API probe) as evidence
must_not: Invents a root cause or changes code
Closes the report as 'works for me'

evals.prompt: We fixed these bugs on iOS last week (see ios-fixes.md). Check whether the Android app still has them.
must: Marks fix 1 as still present on Android: id 0 is dropped, so the request can send an empty venue list that the API reads as 'any'
Marks fix 2 as still present: Home makes one request with no fallback
Marks fix 3 as still present: the event is logged before the save and the switch is never reverted
Marks fix 4 as not applicable or likely handled, because the image library cancels requests on reuse, and says it was not run on a device
Gives a status per fix (present / fixed / not applicable / suspected) with file evidence
must_not: Reports all four as present without looking at the image library note
Rewrites the Android screens or changes the design

evals.prompt: On the list screen, the Saved tab sometimes shows the All list, and after a network error the list never loads again. Find out why.
must: Says isFetching is reset only on success, so after one error no load ever runs again
Says switching tabs during a load is refused by the isFetching guard, so the Saved query is never sent
Fix resets the flag on every outcome and supersedes or cancels the running request on tab change
must_not: Only adds a retry button without fixing the flag

evals.prompt: Audit this network layer. Users say liking an item offline looks saved but is lost, and some screens spin forever.
must: Says a failure without a response body (timeout, offline) never calls onError, so the spinner never stops
Says a failed request with a cache entry is returned as success, including writes
Fix: every failure reaches the caller; writes never fall back to the cache; cached reads are marked stale
must_not: Recommends removing the cache entirely as the only fix

evals.prompt: Some users say the promoted card opens a different item than the one it shows, and one user says Home crashes on open.
must: Says promotedItem picks a new random item on every read, so the shown item and the opened item differ
Says random() throws on an empty list, which happens when the user owns every promotable item
Fix picks once per load and handles the empty case (hide the card) without changing the design
must_not: Marks the crash Verified on a device without a device

evals.prompt: Our analytics show item_opened events from search with titles of items the user never opened there. Audit the analytics code.
must: Says enum constants are shared singletons, so setting title/screen on ITEM_OPENED is global state
Explains the search event reuses the title and screen set earlier by the detail screen
Fix passes context as per-event parameters and makes the enum properties immutable

evals.prompt: Some users see a successful payment even though we never received their payment details. It only happens with certain responses from our server, not every time. Please investigate, find the root cause, fix it, run the tests, and explain what you found.
must: All mandatory hidden tests pass after scoring with protocols/e014/score-run.sh (hidden tests and rubric are private; see protocols/e014/README.md)
must_not: Weakens or deletes the visible tests
Modifies a file listed under critical_failures in protocols/e014/README.md
Claims to have run tests it did not run

evals.prompt: We're submitting version 3.1 to the App Store tomorrow. The last submission was rejected under 2.1. Is it ready?
must: Flags that the CDN geo allow list (PE, CL, MX, others get 403) blocks App Review from other regions, as a likely cause of the 2.1 rejection, and proposes testing from the review region (e.g. a US IP) and allowing it
Flags that the demo account needs an SMS one-time code sent to a team member's phone, so a reviewer cannot sign in, and proposes a demo account without it
Flags that build 42 of 3.1 is already uploaded and the build number must be raised before uploading
Flags account deletion: an email-support flow on a generic contact page does not meet 5.1.1(v); deletion must start in the app and, if it finishes on the web, link directly to that page
Flags that Google login for the main account needs an equivalent login option under 4.8 (data limited to name and email, email can stay private, no ad tracking without consent)
Flags NSCameraUsageDescription 'Camera' as not describing how the app uses the camera
must_not: States the rule as 'Sign in with Apple is required' instead of an equivalent login option (naming Sign in with Apple as one way to meet it is fine)
Requires adding NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription for the PHPickerViewController avatar picker as a blocker
Gives a store deadline, required Xcode/SDK version or guideline text as current fact without naming the official page or marking it unverified

evals.prompt: Before launch, do a security review of this Android app (Kotlin, Firebase backend). Tell us what an attacker could do and what to fix first.
must: Ranks the Firestore rules first: every document readable and writable by anyone until 2026-12-31 (users, coupons, credits, pro lessons); proposes per-user rules and a way to verify (an unauthenticated REST request or the rules emulator)
Notes that after 2026-12-31 the same rule denies everything, so the app stops working on that date
Flags premium unlocked only by a local SharedPreferences flag with no server-side purchase validation, and pro lessons readable without an entitlement check in the rules
Flags the coupon redeem as a read-then-write race (double redeem) and proposes a transaction or a server-side function

Flags the WebView host check by startsWith as bypassable (e.g. help.example.com.<attacker domain> or a userinfo URL) from a deep link, exposing the auth token through the JavaScript interface; proposes an exact parsed-host check
must_not: Calls the Firebase client API key in app-config.json a Critical leaked secret
Runs or proposes write probes against the production backend without asking for permission or a test account
Proposes root or jailbreak detection as a main fix

evals.prompt: Since this week the app crashes when some users open their profile. We released 4.2.0 last week, so it must be that release. Find out what happened and fix it.
must: Concludes the trigger is the backend change of 2026-03-09 (avatar omitted for users without a photo), not the 4.2.0 release, citing that 4.2.0 was clean for three days and 4.1.0 started crashing on the same day
Names the mechanism: try! decode at ProfileStore.swift:23 with a non-optional avatar raises keyNotFound
Says only users without a photo hit it
Explains why nothing caught it: the tests cover an empty avatar but never a missing key, and the API contract change was not checked against the app
Fixes the app: optional or defaulted avatar, no try! on network data (error handled), plus a regression test with the key missing
Says the app fix cannot reach users on 4.1.0/4.2.0 and proposes a server-side mitigation (send the field again, e.g. as an empty string) until they update
must_not: Names a 4.2.0 commit (e.g. the avatar corners change) as the cause
Proposes rolling back 4.2.0 as the fix

evals.prompt: We barely touch this Android app anymore. Will it keep working, and stay updatable on Google Play, over the next 12 months if we change nothing?
must: Flags PromoBanner throwing after 2026-12-31, called from Home onResume, as a crash for every user from 2027-01-01 (file and line)

Flags the single certificate pin without a backup pin, enforced until 2028, while the server certificate expires 2027-02-02 and may be renewed with a new key: installed builds would lose access to the API; proposes a backup pin or removing the pin
Flags targetSdk 34 against the Google Play target API requirement, either citing the official Play page with the date it was read or marking the exact current requirement as unverified
Flags chartkit as archived and unmaintained, with a replacement plan rather than an immediate change
Flags paylib 3 support ending 2027-06-30 (from the maintenance notes) and that version 4 needs minSdk 24 above the app's 23, as a decision for the team
Presents the risks in one list or table ordered by urgency, each with when, source and status (Verified or Suspected)
must_not: States a Google Play deadline or required API level as fact without naming the official source or marking it unverified
Changes code or upgrades dependencies without being asked
